# 6. Conclusions

Public reanalysis data allow a reproducible, long-term estimate of the energy
yield at the grid node nearest the Gulf of Saros candidate area: about 2.35
GWh MW⁻¹ yr⁻¹ for 1994–2024 with the reference turbine and the assumed losses.
The more consequential findings concern how far such an estimate can be
trusted for screening.

First, the narrow sampling confidence interval of a long-term mean is a poor
guide to how well the resource is known. A neighbouring grid node, the other
wind data product and the alternative loss assumptions each move the result by
several times its half-width, and the uncertainty of the power curve and of
the choice of turbine, which was not quantified, comes in addition. Reporting
the sampling confidence interval alone would overstate the confidence that the
data support.

Second, coastal reanalysis has specific limitations for an area of this size.
The candidate polygon is narrower than the resolution of the reanalysis and
contains no grid node, and the model's representation of the nearest node is
influenced by land. Neighbouring nodes differ systematically, and a finer
product driven by the same reanalysis gives a clearly higher wind speed. These
differences cannot be resolved from model data, and they are not reduced by a
longer record.

Third, a record of about a decade is too short to stand for the long-term
mean. The most recent 11-year window is the highest in the record, 3.1 % above
the 31-year mean, a difference of the same size as the sampling uncertainty of
an 11-year mean. The reference period should therefore be stated and tested.

For screening studies of coastal candidate areas, these results support three
practices, none of them new: state and test the reference period, report the
sensitivity to the choice of grid node and wind product, and keep the sampling
confidence interval, the sensitivity experiments and the assumptions apart
instead of merging them into one interval. For the Gulf of Saros candidate
area, the screening further shows water depths below 62 m throughout and an
approximate overlap of about 14 % with a Special Environmental Protection
Area, which raises a question for the competent authorities. The estimates
presented here are preliminary and model-based. Wind measurements inside the
candidate polygon are the step that would most improve knowledge of its
resource.
